# RakNet in FakeBots: what was changed and why

The plugin embeds the RakNet 2.52 fork that open.mp uses for its legacy (SA-MP 0.3.7)
network component: <https://github.com/openmultiplayer/RakNet>, commit recorded in
`UPSTREAM_COMMIT.txt`. It is vendored in this directory (no download at configure time).

That fork is written for a **server**. A bot is a **client**, and a plugin owns *many* clients at
once, so the fork cannot be used unchanged. Everything below is applied by
`tools/apply_raknet_client_patches.py` to a pristine checkout (every replacement is asserted to
match exactly once, so a changed upstream fails loudly). The pristine-vs-patched difference is
therefore reviewable with `git diff` or by re-running the script.

## Replaced files

| File | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `SAMPRakNet.hpp`, `SAMPRakNet.cpp` | The upstream versions need the open.mp SDK (`ICore`, `Query`, ...) and cannot be compiled outside the open.mp tree. The replacements implement the **client side** of the protocol: datagram obfuscation, connection cookie, `ID_AUTH_KEY` lookup, a thread-safe log queue. |
| `SampCryptData.inc` | Generated by `tools/gen_crypt_tables.py`: the 256-byte substitution table (a bijection, so the client can invert it) and the `ID_AUTH_KEY` challenge/response tables of SA-MP and of open.mp. |

## Patches

**`SocketLayer.cpp`**
- Receive: server to client datagrams are plain RakNet. The upstream code decoded every datagram and
  answered `SAMP` queries (server logic).
- Send: every client to server datagram is obfuscated for the destination port, exactly like a
  real client does. The scratch buffer lives on the stack; upstream used one static buffer, which
  corrupts packets as soon as two bots send at the same time.
- `SO_REUSEADDR` is switched off. Linux let two bots bind the *same* ephemeral port; the server
  then saw one peer instead of two and answered the second handshake with "attempt failed".

**`SocketLayer.h`**
- The layer is a process-wide singleton that every `~RakPeer()` deleted (and, on Windows, ran
  `WSACleanup()` for) while the other bots' network threads were still using it. It is now created
  thread-safely on first use and lives until the plugin is unloaded.

**`RakPeer.cpp` / `RakPeer.h`**
- Open-connection request carries `cookie ^ 0x6969` (it used to send an uninitialised byte). The
  server's `ID_OPEN_CONNECTION_COOKIE` reply is stored and the request repeated immediately.
- New `HandleAuthKeyChallenge`: answers the server's `ID_AUTH_KEY` challenge with the matching
  40-character response, on the network thread (the join no longer depends on how busy the
  server's main thread is). A response from the genuine table makes the server treat the
  connection as a normal **player**; the NPC branch of the server-side auth code was removed.
- `ID_NO_FREE_INCOMING_CONNECTIONS` / `ID_CONNECTION_BANNED` from the server cancel the attempt
  at once and are reported to the plugin (upstream retried silently until the attempt limit).
- The "kick whoever did not log on within 30 s" rule is a server rule; it made every bot
  disconnect itself exactly 30 seconds after connecting. It is no longer applied to a connection
  we initiated.
- The number of open-connection attempts is configurable (`SAMPRakNet::SetMaxConnectionAttempts`).

**`ReliabilityLayer.cpp`**, **`RakPeer.cpp`**: diagnostic lines (printed only with `FAKEBOTS_DEBUG=1`).

**`SingleProducerConsumer.h`**: list nodes were allocated as `DataPlusPtr` and freed through a
`char*` (undefined behaviour; AddressSanitizer reported hundreds of `new-delete-type-mismatch`
errors per run).

## Build definition

`RAKNET_LEGACY=1` selects the SA-MP wire format (packet ids and reliability layer). Without it the
original RakNet 2.52 numbering is used and no SA-MP server understands the client.

## Not changed on purpose

Reliability layer, RPC layer, bit streams, string compression: this is the exact code the server runs,
which is why the wire format matches by construction.
